recommendation: Fund playback reliability next quarter, starting with music that stops, pauses or changes on its own, false no-internet errors, and app crashes and freezes. Playback has the highest severity of the large areas, and its complaint share is growing.
memo_markdown:
## Recommendation

**Priority area: playback.** Fund first: (1) music that stops, pauses or changes on its own, (2) false no-internet errors while online, and (3) app crashes, freezes and failed loads.

The baseline ranking puts free-tier restrictions first, but that is largely a monetisation-design choice rather than a defect. Playback is the best place for engineering effort.

## Why

- Playback has 42 complaints [T007] with a mean severity of 3.357143 [T009]. 20 of them are severity 4 or higher [T010]. Usability has 0 such complaints [T022], billing/support has 4 [T004], and other has 0 [T016].
- The three playback issues have severity sums of 42 [C018], 32 [C022] and 32 [C026]. Their mean severities are 3.500000 [C019], 3.555556 [C023] and 4.000000 [C027].
- The trend is upward. Playback complaints rose from 6 of 129 completed records in the early window to 20 of 227 in the late window. Early window share was 4.65% and late window share 8.81% (trend comparison, full months only; the pack gives no claim ID for these figures).

Customer examples:
- "Continously pauses songs and podcasts randomly." [R:f1abd13b-2391-4b04-8109-efa7f3cfed0b]
- "It keeps saying I don't have internet connection while I do, takes FOREVER to look up a song." [R:98d936e1-fd1d-475a-89ee-0e1517cb60d3]
- "Also when I'm playing a playlist from my phone to the Xbox series x it randomly starts playing different music." [R:a0cbc9d6-51bb-46f0-9ba9-ad4f4593c266]

## Alternatives considered

- **Billing/support:** 50 complaints [T001] and a severity sum of 146 [T002], the highest of any area, driven by free-tier restrictions (39 complaints [C001], priority score 116 [C004]). Mean severity is 2.920000 [T003] and only 4 are severity 4+ [T004]. It ranks lower because these complaints are mostly about product policy, not breakage. It would win if leadership wants to revisit free-tier limits, or if revenue data showed these users convert or churn. There are 6 cancellation-language records [T005].
- **Usability:** 54 complaints [T019] with a severity sum of 123 [T020], but mean severity is only 2.277778 [T021] and none are severity 4+ [T022]. Ads (26 complaints [C009]) and layout redesigns (19 [C013]) are annoyances rather than blockers.
- **Access:** the most severe per complaint at a mean of 4.125000 [T033], with 8 complaints [T031]. The volume is too small to lead; login failure alone has 7 [C029]. Worth a small parallel fix.
- **Other/general dissatisfaction:** 62 complaints [T013] at a mean of 2.000000 [T015]. It is not actionable without more detail.

## Limitations

- The data is self-selected public reviews and may not represent all users.
- There is no revenue, plan or churn data. Cancellation language is stated intent, not observed churn.
- Classification coverage: 500 of 500 source rows completed, 21 via exact-text reuse, and 70 flagged as needing review. 236 are complaint or cancellation records.
- Verifier agreement on a 50-review sample was 0.88 for topic, 0.94 for intent, and 0.78 for exact severity (mean absolute error 0.24). Label noise is therefore real, especially for severity.
- The baseline score weights count by severity, so it favours high-volume issues. Ranking playback first relies on its severity profile and trend, not the baseline score alone.
